Patient, reported that all four bottles of the product, DOXA2, supplied to them contained “black specks within the suspension”

On 16 Jan 2026, Eaststone received a complaint from Browns Pharmacy on behalf of a patient, who reported that all four bottles of the product, DOXA2, supplied to them contained “black specks within the suspension” 
(See Appendix 1).

As DOXA2 is manufactured for stock and the patient indicated that all four bottles supplied were affected, all remaining stock of the batch held on site was immediately placed under quarantine. Arrangements were made for the four bottles in the patient’s possession to be returned for visual inspection and confirmation of the reported contamination. To ensure continuity of patient treatment, replacement bottles were sourced externally and supplied to the patient.

On 16 FEB 2026, Eaststone received a complaint from Westpoint Pharmacy on behalf of a patient, who complained that the product of HYDR47 received, was only half full and had a runny consistency.

On 16 FEB 2026, Eaststone received a complaint from Westpoint Pharmacy on behalf of a patient, who complained that the product of HYDR47 received, was only half full and had a runny consistency. 

An initial response was sent out to the customer to acknowledge the complaint and attempt to obtain further information to aid in the investigation and root cause identification. Photographs were requested and arrangements were made for the product to be returned for visual inspection and confirmation of the complaint. (See Appendix 1)

Therefore, a thorough investigation will be conducted to evaluate the circumstances of this complaint, determine validity of the complaint, determine whether any quality related factors may have contributed to the complaint and assess the quality of the product. The investigation will include a review of all relevant batch records, raw materials, storage conditions, complaint history and any available supporting information from the patient or pharmacy. This assessment will be performed in accordance with Eaststone’s Quality Management System and applicable GMP requirements to ensure that any potential root causes are identified and that appropriate corrective and preventive actions are implemented where necessary.

Other

Most probable root cause of this complaint is that as this the first time ordering this product from Eaststone, the patient has raised concerns over the fill quantity and consistency of the product, which may be different to what the patient has received previously from other suppliers. Additionally, no quality defects were found with the product.

Incorrect year on labels for all affected batches

On 17 February 2026, Eaststone received a complaint from Wellbeing Pharmacy regarding product MELA32, reporting that the supplied product was out of date (See Appendix 1).

An initial acknowledgement was sent to the customer and photographic evidence was requested to support the investigation and facilitate root cause identification. Subsequent reviews shortly after identified that a total of 6 batches were affected by an incorrect expiry date printed on the product labels.

Upon confirmation of the labelling error, all impacted customers were formally notified. Customers were instructed to dispose of the affected stock using the material disposal documentation issued by Eaststone, and all affected orders were reprocessed and resupplied to ensure continuity of patient medication.

A comprehensive investigation will be conducted to evaluate the circumstances surrounding this complaint to determine whether any quality related factors contributed to the issue and to assess any potential impact on product quality, safety or compliance. The investigation will include a review of:

•	Batch Manufacturing and Packaging Procedures
•	Label Generation and Approval Procedures
the customer got burning sensation on the body after applying the product

On Wednesday 25th February 2026, a product quality complaint was received from an Alliance customer concerning Gabapentin 6% Gel, batch number BN178593. The pharmacy reported that a patient applied the product and experienced an immediate burning sensation at the site of application. The sensation was described as occurring straight away upon application of the gel. No visible skin changes were reported, and there were no observable signs of dermatological reaction. The complaint specifically relates to the burning sensation experienced during application, with no visible external reaction noted at the time of reporting.
No root cause analysis conducted as complaint was invalid
Missing label on primary packaging of suppositories

On 04 June 2026, Eaststone received a complaint relating to the labelling of Aspirin 300 mg Suppositories (ASPI4). The complaint identified that the suppository mould, in which the product is supplied, was not labelled with the finished product label. Under the current process, suppositories are dispensed within the mould and packaged within a box, where only the box is affixed with the finished product label.

Additionally, on 08 June 2026, another complaint was raised by the same customer for a different suppository product, Chloral Hydrate 500mg Suppositories (CHLO23). This complaint was for the same issue identified in ASPI4.

Following a review of the applicable GMP and regulatory requirements, it was determined that the suppository mould constitutes primary packaging as it is in direct contact with the product. As such, the primary packaging should be appropriately labelled to ensure product identification and traceability. These complaints were therefore confirmed as valid, and a formal investigation was initiated to determine the root cause of this deficiency and identify appropriate corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs) to prevent recurrence.
